approaches_tried_and_rejected: Keeping the bracket scan unconditional and documenting it (first reviewer's Option B): rejected, it breaks the rule that every change of numerical method is an option off unless a registered amendment turns it on.

Folding the bracket option into Amendment 3: rejected, the 2026-10-14 runs do not show the solve defect, and the amendment rule needs a preserved failing run that does; only a registered relax with Amendment 3 alone can show it, so it is a separate Amendment 4.

Source consistency from the whole-package digest: rejected, the package holds modules a Ball run never imports (evolution.py and plotting.py, outside the closure, were edited on 2026-10-13 while this work was going on), which would make a campaign INCONCLUSIVE for unrelated edits. An edit to a closure module (io.py is one) does change the closure digest, as it should.

Closure digest over the qstars modules present in sys.modules at the end of each process: rejected, relax and track processes load different subsets (fold only in track), so equal code would give different digests; replaced by the fixed BALL_MODULES list, imported up front, with a self-check of modules loaded outside it.
Leaving relax.json unwritten on an interrupt (pre-round behaviour): rejected, the directory would have no record; it is written as control_stop and preserved_failure refuses control_stop as evidence.

A first ff_relax.py labelled the run kind 'DRYRUN_relax_...': the new row-0 provenance check refused its row 0 for smoke ('no run.json of kind relax'), as it should; rerun with kind relax under a DRYRUN parent.
